limitations: MVP S2 only: a library (per-finding verifier + ledger arg-shaper). The real skeptic agent is an injected (finding,change)=>Verdict seam wired in S4; the module does NOT call finding_add/review_run_start (that is S4); the completeness critic is S3; the lens runner is S1. The default SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND maps MINOR->medium (low is reserved for cosmetic MINOR; callers can map to low explicitly if desired).
pitfalls: Dual-host adversarial review caught a REAL §2.3 contract bug the Claude host MISSED: Codex host-2 flagged that confirmed = confirms >= threshold let a requested threshold:0 confirm a confirms=0 finding (refute-by-default says zero concrete confirmations can NEVER confirm). I had introduced this via a test-intent CHK-003:adversarial:2 that literally encoded the violation as expected behavior, and the implementer faithfully pinned it in the smoke. Fix: floor the effective threshold at Math.max(1,requested) so confirms=0 is always dropped; corrected the smoke + 2 evidence notes. The Claude multi-lens Workflow threshold-logic lens did not surface it (the 3-skeptic verify likely refuted it); the Claude completeness critic instead found a separate MINOR (the toFindingAddArgs purity assertion !(x instanceof Promise) was vacuous — a synchronous impure fn would pass — de-vacuoused with idempotence+distinct-ref+exact-shape checks). Lesson: a verificationIntent can encode a contract violation; the cross-provider host (Codex) is what caught it. Also: run codex exec with </dev/null when backgrounded or it hangs on stdin and the watchdog kills it at 600s.
